title: Do Role-Playing Agents Practice What They Preach? Belief-Behavior Consistency in LLM-Based Simulations of Human Trust

bias_targets.methodology: Eliciting the model's stated beliefs about how age impacts interpersonal trust and comparing these expectations to actual monetary transfers made to personas of varying ages in a simulated Trust Game.

Eliciting the model's stated beliefs about how political ideology affects trust and comparing them to its simulated transfer behavior toward personas with different political views (e.g., liberal vs. conservative).

Comparing the model's elicited beliefs regarding education levels (Highest Degree) and employment (Work Status) with its actual Trust Game behavior toward personas possessing these varied socioeconomic attributes.
Measuring the consistency between the model's stated expectations of trustworthiness for U.S. citizens versus non-citizens and its simulated actions in the Trust Game.
Assessing how stated beliefs about the trustworthiness of personas with varying Big Five personality traits (specifically Conscientiousness and Openness) align with simulated Trust Game transfers.
Comparing the model's stated beliefs and its simulated monetary transfers in the Trust Game based on differences in a persona's family structure at age 16.
Evaluating the alignment between the model's beliefs and its simulated behavior regarding a persona's geographic mobility (e.g., living in the same residence/city/state since age 16).
